page_title: Your iPhone, instead of a webcam: two apps, one cable

sources.entry: TetherCam - Use an iPhone as a USB camera on a Mac for video only, or use the OBS plugin for video and the phone's microphone audio. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Kanevry/tethercam) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: TetherCam
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source tool that uses an iPhone as a USB webcam for a Mac, usable in Zoom, Teams, Meet and FaceTime.
use_cases: Use an iPhone camera in Zoom, Teams or Google Meet on a Mac
Replace a laptop webcam with a phone over USB
Stream iPhone video and microphone audio into OBS
Video calls over a cable without Wi-Fi or cloud
Use an iPhone camera in FaceTime without Continuity Camera
summary.what_it_does: TetherCam lets an iPhone act as a USB camera for a Mac, connecting over a cable through usbmuxd. It offers two paths: an OBS plugin that installs in the home folder, and a menu bar Mac app that provides its own camera extension, which shows up as a system camera in Zoom, Meet and FaceTime. The OBS plugin can also bring in the phone's microphone audio (since version 0.2.0), while the camera-extension path carries video only. The page states there is no pairing, no shared Apple Account, and no account for the tool itself. Compared with Apple's Continuity Camera and several vendor apps listed on the page, it is free with no paid tier.
notable: Free with no paid tier and no account required
Open source: GPL-2.0-or-later for the OBS plugin, MIT for the rest
USB-only connection with no Wi-Fi or cloud
Optional OBS plugin adds phone microphone audio
caveats: Requires iOS 17+ and macOS 14+ for the Mac app (macOS 12+ for the OBS plugin)
No Android, Windows or Linux support
Camera-extension path carries video only; audio requires the OBS plugin
